text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Hebron deal being "scuttled," say aides to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
- Professor Yitzhak Englard elected to Israel's Supreme Court.
- Rioting continues in Hebron; cameramen hit by army gunfire.
- Tight security as Israel's Maccabiah Games open.
- Industrial exports up 8.1 percent to $9 billion in first half. Job seekers increase 0.8 percent last month to 143,900.
- Tourism Minister Moshe Katzav slams proposal to impose value-added-tax on tourism.
- Israel and European Union sign trade agreements on public procurement and telecommunications.
- Treasury: No comment on reported plan for combined 4 billion shekel cut in 1997.
GLOBES
- Record unemployment in June.
- Government approves programme for joint Israeli-Jordanian airport in Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba.
- Israel releases Palestinian equipment for Gaza airfield.
HAARETZ
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office: We stand before "a propaganda war" with the Palestinain Authority.
- Netanyahu's diplomatic adviser Uzi Arad meets U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross in Washington; makes Israel's ambassador Eliahu Ben-Elissar wait in car.
MAARIV
- "On the verge of explosion" -- This the army assessment of situation in Hebron.
- Unemployment in a year has risen by 23 percent.
- Merrill-Lynch to buy 13 percent of Bezeq from government for $250 million.
- Koor's Stanley Gold warns the conversion law will turn foreign investors away.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Prime minister warns Palestinians: A deterioration will cost you dearly.
- Netanyahu, Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel hold decisive economic talks on Tuesday. Agenda includes tax reform and budget cut.
